learn: A function assigns exactly one output to each input; f(x) names the output.
The domain is all allowed inputs; the range is all outputs.
Exclude inputs that divide by zero or take even roots of negatives.

learn: f(x) + k shifts up k; f(x - h) shifts right h.
-f(x) reflects over the x-axis; a·f(x) stretches vertically when a > 1.
Apply transformations in a logical order: stretch, reflect, then shift.
An inverse undoes a function; swap x and y and solve.
A function has an inverse function if it passes the horizontal line test.
check: If f(x) = x + 2 and g(x) = 3x, f(g(2)) is...
Invertible functions pass the ___ line test.

learn: Solve by graphing, substitution or elimination.
One solution: lines cross. None: parallel. Infinite: same line.
Check solutions in both equations.

lessons.try: Solve x + y = 10 and x - y = 2.

learn: Three equations in x, y, z can be solved by elimination in stages.
Eliminate one variable twice to get a two-variable system.
Back-substitute to find all values.
check: With x + y + z = 6, x = y and z = 2, x is...
lessons.try: Solve x + y + z = 6, x - y = 0, z = 2.

learn: Graph inequalities with shaded half-planes; dashed lines for strict inequalities.
Systems of inequalities form a feasible region.
Linear programming finds the maximum or minimum at a vertex of the region.
check: The overlap of shaded regions is the...
lessons.try: Maximise profit for a bakery with two constraints.

learn: Standard: ax² + bx + c. Vertex: a(x - h)² + k. Factored: a(x - r)(x - s).
The vertex is at x = -b/(2a).
a > 0 opens up; a < 0 opens down.

lessons.try: Convert y = x² - 6x + 5 to vertex form.

learn: Methods: factoring, square roots, completing the square, quadratic formula.
The discriminant b² - 4ac tells how many real roots.
check: A negative discriminant means ___ real roots.

learn: Projectile height: h(t) = -16t² + v₀t + h₀ (feet).
The vertex gives maximum height; roots give landing times.
Fit quadratics to data with regression.
lessons.try: Find the max height of a ball with h(t) = -16t² + 64t.

learn: Complex numbers have form a + bi.
Powers of i cycle: i, -1, -i, 1.
Add and subtract like terms: (2 + 3i) + (1 - i) = 3 + 2i.
Multiply with FOIL and replace i² with -1.
Divide by multiplying by the conjugate.
Quadratics with negative discriminants have complex conjugate roots.
x² + 4 = 0 gives x = ±2i.
The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra: a degree-n polynomial has n roots (counting complex and repeated).
Degree and leading coefficient determine end behaviour.
Even degree: both ends the same way. Odd degree: opposite ends.
A degree-n polynomial has at most n - 1 turning points.
check: A cubic has at most ___ turning points.

learn: Long division and synthetic division divide polynomials.
Remainder Theorem: p(a) is the remainder when dividing by (x - a).
Factor Theorem: (x - a) is a factor if p(a) = 0.
check: If p(2) = 0, then ___ is a factor.
p(x) = x² + 1 has remainder ___ divided by x - 1.

learn: Rational Root Theorem lists possible rational zeros as factors of the constant over factors of the leading coefficient.
Multiplicity: even multiplicity touches the axis; odd crosses.
Sum and difference of cubes: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²).
check: A zero of even multiplicity ___ the axis.

learn: A rational function is a ratio of polynomials.
Vertical asymptotes come from zeros of the denominator not cancelled; holes from cancelled factors.
Horizontal asymptotes depend on comparing degrees.
check: f(x) = (x + 1)/(x - 2) has a vertical asymptote at...

learn: Multiply by the LCD to clear fractions.
Check for extraneous solutions that make denominators zero.
Work problems: rates add (1/a + 1/b = 1/t).
check: Pipes of 3 and 6 hours together take...
lessons.try: Two pipes fill a tank in 3 and 6 hours. How long together?

learn: Solve radical equations by isolating and raising both sides to a power; check answers.
The graph of y = √x starts at the origin and curves right.
y = a·b^x grows if b > 1 and decays if 0 < b < 1.
Percent growth: y = a(1 + r)^t; decay: y = a(1 - r)^t.
Exponential graphs have a horizontal asymptote.
check: 100 growing 10% a year for 2 years is...
y = 2^x has a horizontal asymptote at...
lessons.try: Model a town of 10,000 growing 3% a year.

learn: Continuous: A = Pe^(rt), where e is about 2.718.
More frequent compounding grows slightly faster.
lessons.try: Compare $1,000 at 5% compounded yearly and continuously for 10 years.

learn: Half-life is the time for half a substance to decay.
Amount = initial × (1/2)^(t/h).
Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years.
check: 80 g with a 2-day half-life after 4 days is...
lessons.try: Calculate the remaining amount after three half-lives.

learn: log_b(x) = y means b^y = x.
Common log is base 10; natural log ln is base e.
Logs and exponentials are inverses.
log(ab) = log a + log b; log(a/b) = log a - log b; log(a^n) = n log a.
Change of base: log_b(x) = log x / log b.
Use properties to expand and condense.
Take logs of both sides to solve for an exponent.
2^x = 50 gives x = log 50 / log 2, about 5.64.
Applications: doubling time, pH, decibels, Richter scale.
lessons.try: Find how long $500 takes to double at 6% compounded yearly.

learn: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d.
The sum of n terms: Sₙ = n(a₁ + aₙ)/2.
Arithmetic sequences are linear.
aₙ = a₁·r^(n - 1).
Finite sum: Sₙ = a₁(1 - rⁿ)/(1 - r).
Infinite sum converges to a₁/(1 - r) when -1 < r < 1.
Σ notation compactly writes sums.
Recursive formulas define terms from previous ones.
The Fibonacci sequence: each term is the sum of the previous two.
check: Σ from k = 1 to 4 of k is...

learn: Radians measure angles by arc length: 180° = π radians.
On the unit circle, (cos θ, sin θ) gives coordinates.
Special angles: 30°, 45°, 60° and their multiples.
lessons.try: Label the unit circle with exact values.

learn: y = A sin(Bx) has amplitude A and period 2π/B.
Sinusoidal models describe tides, daylight and sound.
Phase and vertical shifts move the graph.
lessons.try: Model daylight hours over a year with a sine function.

learn: The normal curve is symmetric; 68-95-99.7 percent lie within 1, 2, 3 standard deviations.
A z-score = (x - mean)/SD measures distance from the mean.
Sampling methods and bias affect conclusions.
check: About ___ of data lie within 2 SD.
lessons.try: Find z-scores for test results and interpret them.
